source.located: The tree cites no source for 0.06 / 0.09 / '~56 MeV'. Located and READ: (i) Hoferichter, Ruiz de Elvira, Kubis, Meissner, arXiv:1506.04142 (PRL 115, 092301, 2015) -- the phenomenological sigma_piN = 59.1(3.5) MeV, and its eq.(24) 2/9 + 7/9(f_u+f_d+f_s) = 0.305(9); (ii) FLAG Review 2024, arXiv:2411.04268v3, Sec.10.4.4 eqs.(447)-(450), Tab.3 p.11 -- lattice sigma_piN and sigma_s averages; (iii) Barca, Bali, Collins, arXiv:2412.13138 p.1 -- 'More recent phenomenological determinations, when corrected for isospin breaking effects [3], scatter around 56 MeV' -- the only READ statement that matches the tree's '~56 MeV' label; (iv) Barca et al. arXiv:2609.05989 p.2 -- the isospin-convention correction Delta sigma_piN = 3.1(5) MeV (Hoferichter et al. published_statement: Hoferichter et al. 2015 (1506.04142 p.1, eq.(21)): 'sigma_piN = (59.1 +- 1.9 +- 3.0) MeV = (59.1 +- 3.5) MeV', with sigma_piN = sigma(0), sigma(t) = <N(p')| m-hat(uu+dd) |N(p)>, m-hat = (m_u+m_d)/2 (eq.(6)); and eq.(24) 'sum_{q=u..t} f_q^N = 2/9 + 7/9 (f_u^N + f_d^N + f_s^N) = 0.305 +- 0.009'. FLAG 2024 (2411.04268 eqs.(447)-(450)): 'Nf=2+1+1: sigma_piN = 60.9(6.5) MeV'; 'Nf=2+1: sigma_piN = 42.2(2.4) MeV'; 'Nf=2+1+1: sigma_s = 41.0(8.8) MeV'; 'Nf=2+1: sigma_s = 44.9(6.4) MeV'; p.273: 'there is now a 2.7 sigma difference between the Nf=2+1 and Nf=2+1+1 FLAG averages'; p.274: 'some tension, at the level of around three standard deviations' between the Nf=2+1 average and Hoferichter 23. Barca-Bali-Collins 2412.13138 p.1: phenomenological values 'corrected for isospin breaking effects ... scatter around 56 MeV'.
published_hypotheses: Hoferichter 2015: Cheng-Dashen low-energy theorem D+(0,2M_pi^2) = sigma(2M_pi^2) + Delta_R with |Delta_R| <~ 2 MeV (resonance-exchange estimate, eq.(8)).

Hoferichter 2015: Delta_D - Delta_sigma = -1.8(2) MeV (eq.(12)); isospin-violating corrections from the charged/neutral pion mass difference and virtual photons, f_2 = -0.97(38) GeV^-1, |f_1| <= 1.4 GeV^-1 (eq.(17)); isospin limit defined with the CHARGED pion and the proton mass.

Hoferichter 2015: pionic-atom scattering lengths a^{1/2} = 169.8(2.0), a^{3/2} = -86.3(1.8) x 10^-3 M_pi^-1 (eq.(18)); g^2/4pi = 13.7(2); Roy-Steiner equations valid below s_m = (1.38 GeV)^2 with l_m = 1, driving terms from existing PWAs.
Hoferichter 2015 eq.(24): heavy-quark contribution 2/9(1 - sum_light f_q), light set = u, d, s; f_s taken from lattice (Junnarkar-Walker-Loud 2013), not from the sigma term.

FLAG 2024: sigma_q = m_q <N|qq|N> = m_q dM_N/dm_q (Feynman-Hellmann, eqs.(431)-(433),(446)); isospin limit defined with the NEUTRAL pion (~135 MeV); averages subject to FLAG quality criteria; excited-state (N pi, N pi pi) control 'remains an issue' (p.273) and 'the averages may change' (p.274).
FLAG 2024: sigma_s Nf=2+1+1 obtained by multiplying MILC 12C's <N|ss|N> by the FLAG m_s average; Nf=2+1 average error inflated ~10% for chi^2/dof = 1.23.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this entry. The tree cites no source and no date, so 'what the authors had' is read as what the '~56 MeV' label and the '0.09 with strange' row presuppose. Evidence FOR a data gap: the 0.09 row implies sigma_s = 28 MeV, whereas the FLAG 2024 averages (41.0(8.8), 44.9(6.4) MeV) and Hoferichter eq.(24)'s lattice f_s (40.8 MeV) are higher; with them the tree's own formula wants S = 0.093-0.111, not 0.06, and the scan's top row sits at or below the lower end. Evidence AGAINST it mattering: every conclusion the tree draws from S (K_mu negative and O(1) under both H; nuclear matter displaces the vev downward and >19x above threshold; H1/H2 agreement within 1.3) was recomputed with address.py's own functions over S in [0.0096, 0.12] and holds; only magnitudes move (up to x1.85 in H2 EPS_NUCLEAR, x0.54 in H2 courier source density) and one derived prose range (address.py:86, '3 to 4.5' -> 2.78-2.82). On the external result itself: the phenomenologists did not lack data in the sense M means -- the 1991 value ~45 MeV rose to 59.1 MeV in 2015 precisely BECAUSE new pionic-atom scattering lengths arrived (1506.04142 p.4: 'this effect can be immediately traced back to our modern knowledge of the piN scattering lengths as extracted from pionic atoms'). That is a documented instance of M's thesis (an earlier result moved when data arrived), but it moved an input, not a theorem, and the move is inside the tree's scan. The live lattice-vs-phenomenology tension (~3 sigma) is attributed in the 2024-2026 literature to excited-state contamination on the lattice side, i.e. to a methodological gap being closed, not to missing experimental data; it remains unresolved at the physical point.
grade_evidence: (a) The number 0.06 as sigma_piN/m_p STANDS: 56/938.272 = 0.0597, and '~56 MeV' is the READ phenomenological value in the neutral-pion convention (2412.13138 p.1; 59.1 - 3.1 = 56.0). (b) The H1 structure 2/9 + 7S/9 is re-derived exactly in sympy and is identical to Hoferichter 2015 eq.(24). (c) But the tree USES 0.06 as S in that formula, whose derivation (and eq.(24)) requires S over u, d, s: the strange sigma term is a dropped hypothesis at the adopted value (address.py:452, :830, :943-951; excite.py:402-403). (d) The claimed span of 'the lattice sigma-term range' (address.py:336-338) is narrower than current data: top row 0.09 vs current S_uds centrals up to 0.111. (e) The tree's 'no conclusion here turns on it' was tested and holds for every sign/order conclusion, so this is NARROWED, not WRONG and not DATA-DEPENDENT: no conclusion flips with the moved/contested datum; one derived prose range (address.py:86) and the magnitudes of S-proportional outputs do move. The sigma_piN lattice/phenomenology tension is contested (~3 sigma) but lies inside the band tested.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: S_mid redefined as (sigma_piN + sigma_s)/m_p (~0.10-0.11) with the scan's top raised to cover 0.12, or the S_mid row explicitly scoped as u+d only with strange named as an omitted hypothesis. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a conclusion found that flips inside S in [0.0096, 0.12] (none found here), or a physical-point lattice result far outside that band. To WRONG: only if S were shown to lie where K_mu changes sign (S >= 1), which no datum supports. Reading Hoferichter et al. PLB 843 (2023) (arXiv:2305.07045) at source would convert the 3.1(5) MeV convention shift from restated to READ; it cannot move the grade.
